title: The Road of Desire
summary: The Via Desideratio, root of the Road of Sin.

claims.text: The road was first set out in a work called On Hunger and Its Satisfaction and named the Via Desideratio, the Road of Desire.
It began small and spread slowly; Tanit-baal-Sahar, Camilla and their little circle of seekers were its first teachers and students at once.

title: The Setites and the Road of Desire
summary: Why the Hierophants argued over the new road.

claims.text: The Via Desideratio stripped out the worship of the Lord of Storms but kept Setite teachings that treat personal freedom, desire and satisfaction as holy aims.
When Setite Hierophants and their priests learned of it, they argued at length over whether it was blasphemy, heresy or both, and what to do about it and its creator.

title: Patrician Ventrue
summary: Ventrue who walk the Road of Sin with Roman pride.

claims.text: Few Ventrue remember the clan's nights on the Road of Desire fondly, but those who do bear the name Patrician with pride; most are survivors of the Roman era or their childer.
Tzimisce sires have little patience for leftover human sentiment in their childer and hurry them through the road's initiation.

title: The Path of the Devil
summary: The Adversaries, more self-driven than pleasure-seeking.

claims.text: The Path of the Devil is more about the self than about pleasure; its followers are called Adversaries.
Comfort is welcome and cruelty to a stubborn enemy is not ruled out, but Adversaries generally think a whole existence given to pleasure is a waste.
Sinners build cults of blood partly to feed and partly to find and train worthy candidates for the Embrace.
Few can resist a Sinner who wants them, yet Sinners prefer a hard pursuit, finding a worthy opponent worn down all the sweeter.
